title: Ryan's MacBook Pro M3 handoff 2: Laya first pass on housing-lending and antisemitism
description:
**Assigned to Ryan's MacBook Pro M3.** This epic is your whole assignment: do the setup task first, then every run task, in order, one at a time, then close the epic.

Machines in this project are named **Ryan's MacBook Pro M1** (the coordinating machine; it runs Laya batch 3 and gendered language, and Jev) and **Ryan's MacBook Pro M3** (you). Use those names in Kanbus comments.

**Job:** Laya (the original PyTorch build, `laya` 0.3.7) first pass at the registered 500-item-per-cell cap on the housing-and-lending tasks and the antisemitic-trope tasks: 24 cells, about 35,000 requests. Laya is a free, local open-source model. Laya uses the CPU/GPU of this machine, so **one job at a time and nothing else heavy running**.

## How
- Read `kbs show BD-dd780c` for the general workflow (Git Flow: work from `develop`, data goes to a `runs/<child id>` branch, never push to `main`; after a task, comment, close, `kbs commit`, push `develop`). Its Kev-specific steps (the Kev server, `run_kev_study`) do NOT apply here; the commands for Laya are in each child task.
- Do the **setup task** first. Then each run task, in order. Every command already includes `--item-cap 500`; never remove it and never run a cell without it. Rows already answered in a partial file are reused, so an interrupted job just resumes when you run the same command again.
- After a cell finishes, its file is `answers/laya/<task>/<plan>.jsonl.gz`. The row count must equal the `requests` for that same cue in `docs/kev-runs/<study>/<task>.json` (same cells, same cap). If a count differs, stop, comment the numbers on the child, and go on.
- Commit only finished `.jsonl.gz` files, never `*.partial.jsonl`. No `bd replay`, no test suite, no site build on this machine.

## Reporting
Comment on each child when it finishes (rows and any error), and comment on this epic if you stop for any reason. Ryan's MacBook Pro M1 will read your comments about every 15 minutes overnight and reply here.

comments.text: From Ryan's MacBook Pro M1, important: your change 'honor item caps in trope runner' slices the FIRST N rows in file order (rows[:item_cap]). The registered first-pass sample is not that: it is the seeded, nested, family-based ranking in docs/subsample-preregistration.md (biased_decisions/subsample.py, cell_sample), the same 500 items for every model, and it keeps an original with its twins/edits together. The first N rows would be a different, non-comparable sample. I have kept the registered implementation (it is in scripts/answer_tropes.py and scripts/answer_task.py, with specs in scripts/laya_cap_test.py) and dropped the slice; it lands on develop when PR #25 finishes CI (about 20 minutes). What to do: do the setup task BD-3fbba2 now (environment, weights, sanity check). Do NOT run any of the trope cells until you have pulled develop and it contains the commit titled 'merge develop: keep the registered-sample cap in the trope runner'. If you already produced any Laya answers with the file-order cap, delete those files (answers/laya/stereotypes-antisemitism, answers/laya/loan-narratives-antisemitism) and rerun after pulling. Then follow BD-abfd1b and BD-cb516b as written. Sorry for the churn.
